subject: Lumen Capital — routing isolation ask for enterprise deal
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Lumen Capital — routing isolation ask for enterprise deal

Team —

Quick context: Lumen Capital (prospect) is at procurement stage on a ~ $1.2M ARR commitment and they have an explicit SLO requirement that will be a gating item for legal/procurement unless we can give them a deterministic routing/latency guarantee. Emma (Lumen PM) attached their SLO spreadsheet; key ask summarized below.

What they are requesting:
- Per-tenant routing isolation: ability to pin traffic for a customer to a dedicated routing lane/pool to avoid noisy neighbors during market open.
- Pre-warmed KV/prefix cache for pinned sessions to reduce cold-start p95 to <= 150ms for generation endpoints.
- Optionally a regional pin (us-east) and SLA for p95 latency + 99.9% availability for their primary workload.

Why it matters:
- Procurement flagged this as mandatory for compliance and resiliency (they run trading-assistant features). If we can’t make a reasonable promise, they will walk to an alternate provider.
- Revenue: Deal ID LC-2026-0923, expected commitment: $1.2M ARR, potential expansion.

Attachments: Lumen_SLO_requirements.xlsx, MOU_draft_v2.pdf (shared to procurement).

Ask to product/eng: 1) Feasibility/technical constraints 2) Minimal scoped solution we can present as a binding commercial commitment (even if temporary) 3) Rough ETA and whether we can support an interim manual solution that buys time for a fully automated feature.

Target decision date: EOD Mon, Oct 11 (procurement needs language for MOU).

Thanks — appreciate quick triage.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lumen Capital — routing isolation ask for enterprise deal

Thanks Vanessa — couple of clarifying questions before I scope: 

1) Which model family / token sequence lengths are they planning to use for the SLO? (gpt-large variant, avg seq 512?)
2) Peak QPS and expected concurrency during market open (we need this to estimate KV memory and pre-warm cost).
3) Are they open to a product workaround (dedicated pool + routing tag + manual pre-warm script) vs requiring a code change for per-tenant routing in the control plane?

Notes / initial constraints:
- We already support Dedicated pools, but the runtime does not have a customer-facing toggle to "pin" a tenant into a lane that guarantees warm KV cache across restarts. Building a true per-tenant pin with pre-warm + deterministic placement touches orchestration (2–3 PRs) and KV cache lifecycle (hot path).
- Short-term: we could reserve a dedicated pool and run a pre-warm job for them before market open; this is a manual/on-call operation and would require SRE runbook + billing uplift. That can be done in ~2 weeks if we schedule capacity and write the pre-warm tooling.

If you can get answers to Q1–Q3 I can sketch an ETA.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Dev — thanks, answers inline and forwarding Emma's note below (excerpt).

Q1) Model: They plan to use a trimmed gpt-large variant (approx 20B) for assistant generation, avg sequence ~400 tokens, bursts up to 2k tokens in exceptional cases.
Q2) Peak: They estimate sustained market-open concurrency of 25–35 concurrent sessions and peak burst QPS ~ 80 requests/sec for short windows (~5–10 minutes).
Q3) They are willing to take a short-term manual approach if we can guarantee availability and an explicit runbook and pricing for the service. Procurement prefers an automated capability long-term but will accept a time-limited operational commitment.

Vanessa —

Thanks for the call. Key lines for our legal team:

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Lumen Capital — routing isolation ask for enterprise deal

Thanks for the detail — I pulled the ask into a quick engineering assessment. Summary below; happy to sync.

Scope (short-term vs long-term):
- Short-term (mitigation, 2 weeks): Reserve a Dedicated pool in us-east, create a routing tag for Lumen, and run a pre-warm job that loads the model and warms KV for expected prefixes. Requires SRE + an on-call rotation for market open windows, plus a weekly readiness checklist for the 3-month manual commitment. Work effort: ~1 engineer (runtime/SRE) full-time for 2 weeks to build tooling and runbook.
- Long-term (product change, 6–8 weeks): Add a tenant-pin feature in the control plane to: deterministic placement into a warm lane, lifecycle hooks to manage cache persistence, and an admin API for customers to request pre-warm windows. Work effort: 1-week spike + 3 sprints (cross-team) to ship.

Risk/Tradeoffs:
- Short-term: operationally intensive, higher cost (billing uplift), but fastest to meet procurement.
- Long-term: requires orchestration changes and testing across model families; better customer experience and repeatable.

Commercial suggestion: Offer a funded short-term implementation (implementation fee + short-term premium support) and commit to the product change delivery date in the MOU (we can propose a 6–8 week delivery once MOU is signed). This lets procurement get language they need and preserves our roadmap timelines.

Can we confirm two things so I can write the MOU language: 1) Is Lumen comfortable with a paid implementation + premium support for the 3-month manual commitment? 2) Do we have headroom to reserve the Dedicated pool in us-east for their trial window (Karthik — do you own capacity planning for this account?)

If yes, I can draft the MOU paragraph and an internal RFC for prioritization.

— Neha Kapoor
Product Manager, Serving Platform
Redwood Inference
